pages.title: Judgments
pages.note: No Supreme Court judgment delivered in this window was reported; Monday's reported rulings were orders.

items.caseName: Mamata Banerjee v. Election Commission of India
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice Vipul Pancholi
items.headline: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court tells tribunals to hear deleted voters' appeals first, asks ECI to add tribunals
items.text: The Court asked the ECI, in consultation with the Calcutta High Court Chief Justice, to increase the number of election appellate tribunals and find central premises for them in Kolkata. Appeals by voters excluded from the rolls are to be prioritised, while appeals against inclusions are deferred for now. The ECI must list the Kolkata Municipal Corporation constituencies and prioritise appeals from there within a week; West Bengal must file a reply.
items.why: Directly affects voters struck off the rolls during the special intensive revision.

items.caseName: Shanmugha Arts, Science, Technology & Research Academy (SASTRA) v. The State of Tamil Nadu
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Supreme Court bars coercive action against SASTRA University over 31 acres of government land
items.text: After Tamil Nadu said it would not accept SASTRA's offer of about 30 acres of alternative land and Rs 22 crore towards occupation charges, the Court granted leave and made its earlier interim stay on eviction absolute. The State must file a counter affidavit, and the appeal against the Madras High Court's eviction ruling will be heard finally on merits.
items.why: Eviction of a major private university stays on hold until the final hearing.

items.caseName: Jasir Bilal Wani @ Danish v. National Investigation Agency
items.coram: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar
items.headline: Supreme Court refuses bail to Red Fort blast accused, rejects default bail argument
items.text: The Court dismissed the special leave petition of an accused in the November 2025 Red Fort car explosion and left the Delhi High Court's refusal of bail undisturbed. He had argued that because the FIR came after the BNSS took effect, the UAPA provision allowing custody to be extended to 180 days did not apply. The High Court had read the old CrPC reference in Section 43D(2) UAPA as pointing to Section 187 BNSS.
items.why: Leaves in place the High Court's reading that the UAPA 180-day extension works with the BNSS.

items.caseName: Imran Ahmad v. Shashi Prakash Goyal
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Saharanpur mosque demolition: Supreme Court sends contempt plea over bulldozer judgment to Allahabad High Court
items.text: The Court declined to hear a contempt petition alleging that a century-old mosque in Saharanpur was demolished in breach of its November 2024 bulldozer-action guidelines. It sent the record to the Allahabad High Court to establish the facts first, adding that consequences will follow if a violation is found.

items.caseName: Loganathan v. State of Tamil Nadu
items.coram: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva
items.headline: New Supreme Court bench narrows pan-India unauthorised construction case
items.text: The reconstituted bench disposed of all pending intervention and individual applications and left parties free to go to municipal bodies, tribunals or High Courts. It limited the case to suggestions from States and Union Territories on curbing building bye-law violations, asked for their affidavits, and said it would not monitor individual demolitions. Next listed on 6 January 2027.
items.why: Ends the Supreme Court's direct monitoring of individual building-violation cases nationwide.

items.caseName: Abdul Raheman Dhantiya v. The State of Gujarat
items.coram: Justice M.M. Sundresh, Justice Prasanna B. Varale
items.headline: Godhra train burning case: Supreme Court suspends life sentence of convict on medical grounds
items.text: With Gujarat raising no objection to relief confined to medical grounds, the Court suspended the life sentence of a 2002 Godhra train burning convict who has served about 18 years. The trial court will set the conditions, and the merits of the appeal were not addressed.

items.caseName: DCIT v. RIL
items.coram: Justice P.S. Narasimha, Justice Alok Aradhe
items.headline: Supreme Court upholds quashing of reassessments against merged Reliance entities
items.text: The Court dismissed the Income Tax Department's appeal against a February 2025 Bombay High Court ruling. The High Court had held void the assessments for 1993-94 to 1995-96 issued in the names of Reliance Polyethylene and Reliance Polypropylene, which had already merged into Reliance Industries, noting the assessing officer knew of the merger.
items.why: Reaffirms that tax proceedings against a company that no longer exists after amalgamation are invalid.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Supreme Court issues notice on PIL seeking anti-defection law reforms
items.text: On a PIL by A Sethu, the Court sought responses from the Centre, the Election Commission, the Law Commission and the Law and Parliamentary Affairs ministries. The petition asks that a legislator's resignation should not automatically end pending disqualification proceedings, and that Speakers decide on the genuineness of resignations through reasoned, time-bound orders.
items.why: Could tighten how resignations are used to escape disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh
items.headline: Plea against politicians' remarks on judiciary sent to CJI for placing before Justice Datta-led bench
items.text: On a petition by two advocates naming the Centre, the Election Commission, the Congress and several political leaders as respondents, the bench felt it should be heard by the bench led by Justice Dipankar Datta, which is already hearing contempt proceedings over remarks against the CJI. The registry was told to place the papers before the Chief Justice; the merits were not addressed.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Supreme Court dismisses PIL on Uttar Pradesh municipal electoral rolls; correction right is personal
items.text: The Court dismissed a PIL by Ruchi Kaushik seeking corrections to Uttar Pradesh municipal electoral rolls over mismatched house numbers. It said the right to correct an entry belongs to each voter and generally cannot be pursued collectively through a PIL, and that affected voters can approach the election authorities.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Delhi pollution: Supreme Court weighs allowing only BS-VI vehicles, seeks status reports from NCR States
items.text: The Court said it is considering allowing only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not the whole NCR, and floated keeping commercial vehicles out of the city in favour of clean last-mile transport; no formal direction was issued. Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh were asked to file status reports on steps to cut particulate pollution.
items.why: Signals possible restrictions on older vehicles in Delhi.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Kalyani family dispute: Supreme Court suggests arbitration after mediation fails
items.text: Told that mediation led by former judge L. Nageswara Rao had failed, the Court urged the parties in the dispute between Babasaheb Kalyani and his sister Sugandha Hiremath to try arbitration covering family property and corporate matters. It offered to suggest a mutually acceptable arbitrator and listed the case after two weeks.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: CJI Surya Kant recuses from Supertech homebuyers' plea; special bench to be formed
items.text: The CJI recused from a plea concerning Supertech's insolvency and homebuyers, in which orders had been reserved on 16 November, because one applicant is known to him. He said a special bench will be constituted to hear it.

items.caseName: Sunil vs. State of U.P. and 5 Others
items.headline: SDM pulled up for appearing from drawing room; review orders quashed
items.text: The Court sought explanations from the Chitrakoot SDM (Judicial) and the DM after the SDM appeared by video from his home. It quashed two unreasoned review orders in a pradhan election dispute, ordered the review to be decided afresh within four weeks, and sent its order to the Chief Secretary (Panchayati Raj) to consider an inquiry.

items.caseName: Sri Krishna Agrawal vs. State of U.P. and Another
items.headline: An advocate's online article is not law, Court tells counsel
items.text: The Court faulted counsel for relying on another advocate's online article and on a Supreme Court ruling that hurt his own case. It dismissed the criminal revision against refusal of an FIR over unpaid sale consideration, noting the deeds recorded full payment and any bounced cheque falls under Section 138 NI Act.

items.caseName: M/s Shiv Anant Enterprises v. State of U.P. and 3 others
items.coram: Justice Prakash Padia and Justice Indrajeet Shukla
items.headline: Highest bidder has no vested right before formal contract
items.text: The Division Bench held that a bidder, even the highest one, only has a right to fair treatment until a formal contract is made, so cancellation of the tender could not be challenged. It found no mala fides but let the petitioner submit fresh consent within a week to do the work at the earlier lowest rate.

items.caseName: Sadanand and others v. Kalu
items.headline: Executant's illness alone does not prove mental incapacity
items.text: The Court held that illness of the person signing a sale agreement does not shift the burden of proof; the party alleging fraud must first show impaired capacity and domination of will. It allowed the appeals, dismissed the suit to cancel the registered agreement, and decreed specific performance.

items.caseName: Ravindra Kumar Tripathi v. Board of Revenue and others
items.headline: Confirmed revenue auction cannot be reopened on belated objections
items.text: Once an auction is confirmed under Section 174 of the U.P. Land Revenue Act, 1901, the Commissioner cannot set it aside on late objections of irregularity, the Court held. It quashed the Commissioner's and Board of Revenue's orders, leaving parties free to sue for fraud under Section 175.

items.caseName: Rakesh Kumar Pathak and another v. The State of U.P. and 4 others
items.headline: Legal heir need not physically possess land to seek mutation
items.text: The Court held that 'possession' under Section 33 of the U.P. Revenue Code means legal, not physical, possession. It declined to disturb orders recognising a claimed son of the deceased in revenue records, while leaving the brothers free to contest heirship in regular proceedings.

items.caseName: Sri Gopi Kishan Khandelwal v. Smt Archana Tripathi
items.headline: No additional defence after trial begins without due diligence
items.text: The Court dismissed an Article 227 petition by a defendant who, after final arguments in an eviction suit, sought to plead a pre-suit partition. He gave no explanation of how or when he learned of it, so due diligence was not shown.

items.caseName: VKN v. SRT
items.coram: Justice Prakash Padia and Justice Indrajeet Shukla
items.headline: Father's duty to fund education shared with earning mother; share reduced
items.text: The Division Bench held both parents share the cost of supporting a child, and the mother's income can be weighed. It rejected the father's plea that his duty depended on custody, but cut his monthly share from Rs 15,000 to Rs 12,000 and ordered arrears cleared within two months.

items.caseName: Abhishek Banerjee v. State of West Bengal
items.headline: Abhishek Banerjee's protection from arrest in six cases extended to 26 Feb 2027
items.text: The Court extended interim protection from coercive action for the TMC MP in six criminal cases until 26 February 2027 or further orders. It noted that investigations were incomplete, that the State's SLP against the earlier order was lying in defect, and that circumstances had not changed.

items.caseName: Naresh Kumar Gupta & Anr. v. State NCT of Delhi & Anr.
items.headline: Later complaint cannot cure cognizance taken on police chargesheet under PCPNDT Act
items.text: The Court held that Section 28 of the PCPNDT Act bars cognizance except on a complaint by the Appropriate Authority, and this defect goes to the Magistrate's jurisdiction. A subsequent complaint by the Authority cannot regularise cognizance taken on a police chargesheet. The cognizance order was set aside and the Magistrate told to consider the Authority's complaint afresh.

items.caseName: Payal v. Pooja Gupta
items.headline: PG accommodation is a licence, not a lease; Rent Control Act inapplicable
items.text: The Court said a paying guest only uses a room while the operator keeps overall control, so the arrangement is a licence. It dismissed the PG resident's second appeal against a possession decree, holding she could not claim Delhi Rent Control Act protection. An unregistered plain-paper agreement to buy rooms gave her no right to stay.

items.caseName: Deepak Tyagi v. Bar Council of India
items.headline: BCI suspension of lawyer in Justice Talwant Singh incident quashed
items.text: The Court quashed the Bar Council of India's interim suspension of the advocate over his conduct towards returning officer Justice Talwant Singh during the Bar Council of Delhi polls. He had apologised unconditionally and undertaken not to repeat the conduct, and Justice Singh accepted the apology, so continuing action served no purpose.

items.caseName: N.Y. v. R.K.Y. and Others
items.headline: Senior Citizens Act authorities may order daughter-in-law's relocation, with safeguards
items.text: The Court held tribunals under the Senior Citizens Act can direct a daughter-in-law to leave a shared household where needed to protect elderly parents, but only after balancing competing rights. It upheld relocation in principle and replaced open-ended directions with fixed terms, including rent and deposit to be paid by the parents-in-law and restoration of possession on default.

items.caseName: A & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.
items.headline: Amritsar passport office location no bar to Delhi HC hearing plea against CARA
items.text: Adoptive parents sought a CARA no-objection certificate so their adopted daughter could move to Australia. The Court rejected the territorial-jurisdiction objection, holding that the passport office being in Amritsar does not oust its jurisdiction over relief sought against CARA. The matter is listed for arguments on merits on 2 December 2026.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Qadeemi Masjid: Waqf Board told to answer worshipper's representation in four weeks
items.text: In the plea to retain Qadeemi Masjid in the Krishi Bhawan compound amid Central Vista redevelopment, the Delhi Waqf Board argued the mosque is notified waqf property. The Court directed the Board to reply to a worshipper's representation within four weeks and listed the matter in January 2027. No interim restraint on demolition was reported.

items.caseName: Om Parkash and another v. Anita and others
items.headline: Father and sisters of deceased bachelor not dependants for accident compensation
items.text: In a motor accident appeal, the Court held that only the mother of the unmarried deceased was a dependant, excluding the father and sisters. Applying a 40% future-prospects addition, it reduced the award from about Rs 17.2 lakh to Rs 11.79 lakh, payable to the mother.

items.caseName: Zaffer Ul Khan @ Zaffer Ullah Khan v. Member, J&K Special Tribunal, Jammu & Ors.
items.headline: Long possession and utility bills cannot save illegal construction
items.text: The Court dismissed in limine a challenge to a demolition notice under the J&K Control of Building Operations Act, 1988. Long occupation, utility bills and investment do not confer ownership or shield a structure built without approved plans, and disputes about the building's age belong in civil court.

items.caseName: Sri Farooq Mugili vs State of Karnataka & Another
items.headline: Motorcycle rally raising political slogans not an unlawful assembly without common object
items.text: The Court quashed proceedings against the petitioner, holding that 150-200 people on motorcycles shouting slogans do not form an unlawful assembly under Section 141 IPC without a shared unlawful object. The mahazar showed no property damage and witness statements did not support the alleged violence.

items.caseName: Raja Hussain @ Raja @ Hussain vs. State of Karnataka & Another
items.headline: Woman's marital history no ground to disbelieve cruelty complaint
items.text: The Court said a complainant's previous marriages cannot by themselves discredit a cruelty allegation; only the presence of the offence's ingredients matters. It nonetheless quashed the Section 498A case because the allegations were bald and omnibus, adding that a chargesheet cannot cure a complaint that discloses no offence.

items.caseName: High Court of Karnataka v. Siddesh H & Others
items.coram: Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K S Hemalekha
items.headline: Contempt against lawyers who disrupted CJ's court during strike call closed
items.text: The Division Bench accepted the unconditional apology of advocates accused of disrupting a hearing in the Chief Justice's court while urging lawyers to join a strike over attacks on advocates. Finding the apology sincere, it discharged them and closed the suo motu contempt case.

items.caseName: Archana P.S. and Ors. v. Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady and Ors.
items.headline: Student protest cannot be crushed by career-ending punishment
items.text: Disposing of a plea by 16 suspended students, the Court set aside the suspension, the inquiry committee, its report and the punishment order. It treated the roughly 84 days already spent under suspension as punishment, allowed fresh proceedings but barred re-suspension, and directed separate exams for the students within six weeks.
items.why: Affirms that universities may curb violent protest but cannot use discipline to silence dissent.

items.caseName: Theeran Thirumurugan @ Thirumurugan v. State of Tamil Nadu and Another
items.headline: FIR over video criticising CM's Karur job policy quashed
items.text: The Madurai Bench quashed the case against a man who posted a video criticising Chief Minister Vijay's decision to give government jobs to families of Karur stampede victims. Though the language was improper, the video was political comment with no incitement or false claim, so offences under Sections 352 and 353(2) BNS were not made out.

items.caseName: P Rajasekaran v. Deputy Director, ED
items.coram: Justice GR Swaminathan and Justice P Vadamalai
items.headline: ED need not separately prove likelihood of concealment to attach proceeds of crime
items.text: The Division Bench held that once the ED has material to believe a person holds proceeds of crime, it need not separately show a likelihood of concealment before provisional attachment under Section 5(1) PMLA. Appeals arising from the Madurai granite quarrying case were dismissed and the attachment upheld.

items.caseName: R Thrishuli v. The State and Others
items.headline: Plea for FIR against TVK MLA: State asked to verify if Collector complained
items.text: Hearing a plea seeking an FIR against Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh over alleged obscene messages to a woman Collector, the Court indicated it would not order an FIR absent her complaint. It directed the State Public Prosecutor to obtain instructions from the Chief Secretary and the Collector, and adjourned the matter to 24 November.

items.caseName: Shyam Singh Chauhan vs. Central Bureau of Investigation
items.headline: Gravity of corruption alone no reason to refuse suspension of fixed-term sentence
items.text: The Court suspended the four-year sentence of an official convicted in a 2017 CBI bribery trap case, pending his appeal. It held that the seriousness of a corruption offence cannot by itself justify refusal, noting he had been on bail for about nine years without misuse.

items.caseName: Kulwant Singh v State of Punjab
items.headline: Punjab to pay Rs 1 lakh to man challaned under NDPS for non-narcotic tablets
items.text: The Court quashed the NDPS FIR over 550 Tapentadol tablets after the salt was found not to be a narcotic, and ordered Rs 1 lakh compensation. It faulted the State for filing a challan despite that finding and called departmental action against the investigating officer a token step.

items.caseName: Virendra Agrawal v. The Election Committee, Rajasthan High Court Bar Association, Jaipur & Ors.
items.headline: Bar association can require proof of active practice to vote
items.text: The Jaipur Bench quashed the Election Committee's 17 November notice dropping the two-vakalatnama or two-order-sheet condition for voters, and restored the earlier notices. It held the requirement reasonable, observing that mere continued membership should not confer voting rights.

items.caseName: Smt. C. Rajya Lakshmi v. Sri Thoka Venkateswarlu & Ors
items.headline: 120-day written statement limit applies only to commercial suits
items.text: The Court ruled that the 120-day cap under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC governs commercial disputes, not ordinary civil suits. Time taken by the trial court to decide a plaint-rejection application, pending here for about five years, cannot be held against the defendant. The trial court's order refusing the written statement was set aside.
items.why: Defendants in ordinary suits cannot be shut out for delays caused by the court itself.

items.caseName: Aerrabolu Venkataiah and another v. Aerrabolu Lingaiah and others
items.headline: Agency court cannot decide land dispute between non-tribals
items.text: The Court found both parties to the agricultural land dispute were non-tribals and no tribal interest was involved, so the Agency Court's special jurisdiction did not apply. It set aside the injunction and police-protection orders passed by the Agency Divisional Officer, Achampet, and directed return of the plaint for filing before the competent civil court.

items.court: Sessions Court, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
items.caseName: State of Delhi v Shubham Tyagi
items.headline: Bail denied to PG operator in Satya Niketan building collapse
items.text: The court refused regular bail to an advocate who operated the PG building that collapsed on 6 September, killing seven people. It found he could foresee the danger from illegal construction, had control as the tenant, and might threaten witnesses as the trial is at an early stage.

items.court: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Saket Court, Delhi
items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Non-bailable warrant issued against Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
items.text: A Delhi magistrate issued a non-bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 criminal defamation complaint by Vikas Pandey over a video. Earlier summons and a bailable warrant had gone unserved as Rathee mainly lives abroad. The matter is next listed on 3 December.

items.court: Additional District and Sessions Court, Taliparamba, Kerala
items.caseName: The Station House Officer v. T.P. Biju and Others
items.headline: Three convicted, 16 acquitted in CPI(M) leader CV Dhanraj murder case
items.text: The court convicted three accused of murder in the 2016 killing of CPI(M) leader C.V. Dhanraj but cleared them of conspiracy and rioting charges. The other 16 accused were acquitted for want of evidence, with the court criticising the probe as mechanical. Sentencing is posted for 25 November.
